This is the most important prompting update for anyone using Astra.

Bookmark this before your next build.

Most people are still prompting Astra like GPT-5. That's the mistake.

→ audit your AGENTS.md — old instructions now fight the model
→ define autonomy explicitly — Astra pauses when you expect it to continue
→ cut skill descriptions to one line — too many skills and Astra sees none of them clearly
→ stop telling it to run tests — it does this automatically, repeating it causes overtesting
→ define stop conditions — Astra needs to know what "done" means

Astra is at its best when you stop micromanaging and let it own the work.

Everyone is posting Astra demos. Almost nobody is posting how the demos were actually run.

The GPT-6 Astra Operating Manual: 4 roles, 4 copy-paste payloads, 1 routing table, 3 facts that change everything.

The three facts. It runs long by design — 128K output, effort from low to max, no off switch. It asymptotes: gets 80% there, then stalls in the minutiae because nobody told it what done means. And it bills like a frontier model with two cliffs: $10/$50, cached input $1, and everything doubles past 272K input tokens.

The four roles. The Manager writes the checklist and phases and never implements. 

The Implementer runs one phase at a time — "completely, extremely well" — and reports back. 

The Verifier checks the phase in a fresh context. 

The Watcher is a checklist page that charts progress, so the loop notices when it has stopped moving.

The routing table. Astra for long builds, computer use, math, 3D. Fable 5.1 for reviewing the code and for cache-heavy loops. Same price. Route by strength.

The guardrail nobody mentions: you cannot read Astra's reasoning anymore. Verify outputs, not thoughts.
